Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure matches the report “Some multi-iterator parsing peek sequences incorrectly consume elements.” The test’s third scenario demonstrates the bug:

- The parser is created on the input "1\n2\n3\n4\n5\n".
- First enhanced for loop over parser breaks after consuming 2 records (values “1”, “2”). This advances the shared CSVParser’s internal lexer by two records.
- Then parser.iterator().hasNext() is called, creating a brand-new Iterator which peeks. In CSVParser.iterator(), hasNext() does:
  - if (this.current == null) this.current = this.getNextRecord();
  - getNextRecord() calls CSVParser.this.nextRecord() (lines 526–542, 547–555), which advances the shared parser by one record and stores it in the iterator’s private current field.
- This iterator is then discarded without calling next(), so the prefetched record (“3”) is stranded inside that iterator’s private buffer.
- The subsequent enhanced for loop creates yet another new iterator and starts from the next record from the shared parser, which is now “4” instead of “3”, breaking the expected sequence.

Root cause in code:
- CSVParser.iterator() returns a new iterator each time (line 523) with an iterator-local buffer current.
- Iterator.hasNext() peeks by consuming a record from the shared CSVParser via CSVParser.this.nextRecord() (lines 536–545), but caches it only in the iterator-local current.
- There is no parser-level lookahead cache in CSVParser; repeated creation of iterators means a hasNext() call on a temporary iterator permanently advances the underlying lexer and makes that record inaccessible to subsequent iterators.

Why the other scenarios pass:
- Within a single iterator, hasNext() prefetches into that iterator’s own current and next() returns it, so no loss occurs.
- Consecutive for-each loops without an intervening hasNext() on a separate iterator do not strand a prefetched record.

Thus, the bug is that hasNext() on a newly created iterator peeks by advancing the shared parser and stores the peeked record only in that iterator’s private state, causing the next iterator to skip that record.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
